rituals.target_pattern: Thought monopolising attention
rituals.precise_subpattern: Thought monopolising attention
rituals.vibeLine: Your thought got bumped from the VIP lane by a moving shadow.
rituals.hook: Find one thing already moving.
rituals.predict: Guess whether you can follow it through three changes without losing the thought completely.
rituals.play: Pick a cursor, fan, shadow, leaf, person, reflection—anything moving. Track three changes: direction, speed, shape, position, brightness.
rituals.catch: Now try to recall the exact wording of the thought from before the third change.
rituals.reveal: The thought may still exist, but it lost uninterrupted access to the attention channel.
rituals.mindBend: Your thought didn’t disappear. It just lost exclusive access to you.

rituals.name: PERIPHERAL DOOR
rituals.title: PERIPHERAL DOOR
rituals.targetPattern: Narrow visual attention under arousal
rituals.target_pattern: Narrow visual attention under arousal
rituals.precise_subpattern: Narrow visual attention under arousal
rituals.vibeLine: Stress cropped the frame. You just uncropped it.
rituals.hook: Stress loves a tunnel.
rituals.predict: Guess how many objects you can notice at the edges without moving your head.
rituals.play: Keep your gaze softly on one point. Without turning, name the farthest thing you can detect on the left, right, above and below.
rituals.catch: Feel whether the scene becomes wider than the problem in the centre.
rituals.reveal: Widening visual attention can compete with the narrow attentional style of threat.
rituals.mindBend: A narrowed mind often arrives with a narrowed field of view.
rituals.ritualCard:

cheeky.reveal: Widening visual attention can compete with the narrow attentional style of threat.
cheeky.mindBend: A narrowed mind often arrives with a narrowed field of view.

rituals.name: SOUND UNTIL IT CHANGES
rituals.title: SOUND UNTIL IT CHANGES
rituals.targetPattern: Assuming sensations stay constant
rituals.target_pattern: Assuming sensations stay constant
rituals.precise_subpattern: Assuming sensations stay constant
rituals.vibeLine: Even the annoying hum cannot stay consistent.
rituals.hook: Choose one sound and wait for it to betray its own sameness.
rituals.predict: Guess how long it will stay exactly the same.
rituals.play: Pick a continuous sound: aircon, traffic, hum, rain, fridge. Listen only for the first change in pitch, volume, rhythm or distance.
rituals.catch: Catch the moment “constant” becomes obviously variable.
rituals.reveal: Attention reveals micro-changes that a stressed brain compresses into “this is just how it is.”
rituals.mindBend: What feels continuous is often changing underneath your label for it.

rituals.name: JAW CONTRAST
rituals.title: JAW CONTRAST
rituals.targetPattern: Unnoticed voluntary amplification of arousal
rituals.target_pattern: Unnoticed voluntary amplification of arousal
rituals.precise_subpattern: Unnoticed voluntary amplification of arousal
rituals.vibeLine: Your jaw needed a before-and-after photo.
rituals.hook: Make tension obvious on purpose so release has something to compare with.
rituals.predict: Guess whether your jaw is already closer to “soft” or “clenched.”
rituals.play: Gently clench your jaw for three seconds—no pain—then let it hang loose. Do nothing else.
rituals.catch: Notice which state suddenly becomes easier to identify because you created contrast.
rituals.reveal: The nervous system notices differences better than vague instructions to “relax.”
rituals.mindBend: Sometimes calm is easier to find after you show the body what “not calm” feels like.

rituals.vibeLine: Nothing multiplied. Your attention got a search filter.
rituals.hook: Pick a colour.
rituals.predict: Guess how many objects of that colour you will notice in ten seconds.

rituals.reveal: Once the brain sets a search target, matching information suddenly feels more frequent.
rituals.mindBend: What you notice more is not always what exists more.

rituals.target_pattern: Body sensation instantly given emotional meaning
rituals.precise_subpattern: Body sensation instantly given emotional meaning
rituals.vibeLine: Pulse first. Plot twist later.
rituals.hook: Find a body signal and ban the biography for ten seconds.
rituals.predict: Guess whether you can describe the sensation without using an emotion word.
rituals.play: Notice your pulse, chest, throat or stomach. Describe only physical properties: fast, slow, tight, warm, fluttery, heavy, moving. No “anxious,” “bad,” “dangerous,” or “because.”
rituals.catch: Catch how quickly the mind tries to add an explanation.
rituals.reveal: Sensation and interpretation arrive close together, but they are not the same event.
rituals.mindBend: Your body can send a signal before your story decides what it means.

rituals.name: ONE-JOINT WEATHER
rituals.title: ONE-JOINT WEATHER
rituals.targetPattern: Posture unnoticed as part of emotional state
rituals.target_pattern: Posture unnoticed as part of emotional state
rituals.precise_subpattern: Posture unnoticed as part of emotional state
rituals.vibeLine: One joint moved and the mood had to renegotiate.
rituals.hook: Change exactly one joint and see if the emotional weather notices.
rituals.predict: Guess whether moving only your shoulders, hands or jaw will change anything at all.
rituals.play: Freeze your current posture. Rate its tension from 0–10. Change one joint only—drop shoulders, uncurl hands, uncross ankles. Re-rate.
rituals.catch: Look for even a one-point change without trying to “feel better.”
rituals.reveal: Body configuration is one ingredient in state, not merely a passive result of it.
rituals.mindBend: You do not have to change your whole mood to change one ingredient.

Freeze your current posture. Rate its tension from 0–10. Change one joint only—drop shoulders, uncurl hands, uncross ankles. Re-rate.
Guess whether moving only your shoulders, hands or jaw will change anything at all.
Look for even a one-point change without trying to “feel better.” Body configuration is one ingredient in state, not merely a passive result of it.

rituals.name: HALF-SPEED HANDS
rituals.title: HALF-SPEED HANDS
rituals.targetPattern: Subjective speed mistaken for objective deadline
rituals.target_pattern: Subjective speed mistaken for objective deadline
rituals.precise_subpattern: Subjective speed mistaken for objective deadline
rituals.vibeLine: Your urgency hated that. Reality seemed fine.
rituals.hook: Do one ordinary movement at half speed and see whether the deadline explodes.
rituals.predict: Guess what will happen if your hands move slowly for fifteen seconds.
rituals.play: Pick a harmless action—put down a cup, type one short sentence, fold a tissue—and do it at deliberately half your normal speed.
rituals.catch: Check if urgency rises, falls, or simply complains while time keeps moving normally.
rituals.reveal: The feeling of rush can persist even when slower behaviour causes no consequence.
rituals.mindBend: Urgency is a sensation. A deadline is a fact. They sometimes travel separately.

rituals.vibeLine: Breathing continued without a management meeting.

rituals.predict: Guess whether breathing will become unsafe, chaotic, or simply continue if you stop managing it for three breaths.

rituals.title: FOREGROUND / BACKGROUND SWAP
rituals.targetPattern: One sound dominating the sensory field
rituals.target_pattern: One sound dominating the sensory field
rituals.precise_subpattern: One sound dominating the sensory field
rituals.vibeLine: Loud sound got demoted without HR paperwork.
rituals.hook: Let’s move one sound out of the starring role without making it stop.
rituals.predict: Pick the loudest sound. Guess whether it still feels dominant after you deliberately promote a quieter sound.
rituals.play: Listen to the loudest sound for five seconds. Find the faintest sound you can detect and give only that sound five seconds of attention.
rituals.catch: Check if the loud sound changed—or whether your attention changed its rank.
rituals.reveal: Sensory dominance is partly about volume and partly about where attention points.
rituals.mindBend: You do not always need silence; sometimes you need a different foreground.

Let’s move one sound out of the starring role without making it stop.
unfiltered.ritualCard:
Let’s move one sound out of the starring role without making it stop.
Listen to the loudest sound for five seconds. Find the faintest sound you can detect and give only that sound five seconds of attention.
Pick the loudest sound. Guess whether it still feels dominant after you deliberately promote a quieter sound.
Check if the loud sound changed—or whether your attention changed its rank. Sensory dominance is partly about volume and partly about where attention points.
↻ FOREGROUND / BACKGROUND SWAP
unfiltered.fullVersion:
Still · Calm · FOREGROUND / BACKGROUND SWAP
VIBE: UNFILTERED

Nothing shut up. Attention just changed the damn pecking order.

HOOK
Let’s move one sound out of the starring role without making it stop.

PREDICT
Pick the loudest sound. Guess whether it still feels dominant after you deliberately promote a quieter sound.

PLAY

CATCH
Check if the loud sound changed—or whether your attention changed its rank.

REVEAL
Sensory dominance is partly about volume and partly about where attention points.

MIND BEND
You do not always need silence; sometimes you need a different foreground.

MOVE ON

rituals.name: CONTACT POINT MAP
rituals.title: CONTACT POINT MAP
rituals.targetPattern: Body treated as one undifferentiated stress signal
rituals.target_pattern: Body treated as one undifferentiated stress signal
rituals.precise_subpattern: Body treated as one undifferentiated stress signal
rituals.vibeLine: Stress said “everything.” Your chair would like to object.
rituals.hook: Your body is touching the world in more places than the worry is reporting.
rituals.predict: Guess how many contact points you can feel without moving.
rituals.play: Count distinct places where your body meets something: feet, chair, clothing, phone, floor, backrest, air on skin. Stop at seven or when you run out.
rituals.catch: Check if the body feels like one solid block or a collection of separate sensations.
rituals.reveal: Granularity changes experience even when nothing is removed.
rituals.mindBend: “My whole body feels bad” can contain many neutral contact points the alarm forgot to mention.

rituals.targetPattern: Global body state masking local variation
rituals.target_pattern: Global body state masking local variation
rituals.precise_subpattern: Global body state masking local variation
rituals.vibeLine: Apparently your hand refused the single-weather narrative.
rituals.hook: One hand contains several tiny climates.
rituals.predict: Guess which finger feels warmest before you compare them.
rituals.play: Touch thumb to each fingertip one at a time. Notice relative warmth, coolness, dryness, pressure or texture. No need to name the exact temperature.
rituals.catch: See whether your first prediction matched the actual pattern.
rituals.reveal: Sensation becomes more detailed when attention stops asking only “good or bad?”
rituals.mindBend: Your body is not one weather icon.

rituals.target_pattern: Near sounds treated as more important
rituals.precise_subpattern: Near sounds treated as more important
rituals.vibeLine: Same sounds, completely different filing system.
rituals.hook: Your ears know distance even when your thoughts do not.
rituals.predict: Guess whether you can find one sound closer than your body and one farther than the room.

rituals.vibeLine: You were apparently co-managing gravity.
rituals.hook: Let gravity do one job for free.
rituals.predict: Guess whether your resting hands are actually resting.
rituals.play: Place both palms somewhere supported. For five seconds, stop pressing down or holding them up. Let the surface carry their full weight.
rituals.catch: Catch any tiny urge to keep helping gravity.
rituals.reveal: The body can maintain unnecessary effort even when support is already available.
rituals.mindBend: Support only works when you let some weight arrive.

rituals.vibeLine: Your thoughts did twelve laps. The clock moved ten seconds.
rituals.hook: Your mind can sprint while the second hand strolls.
rituals.predict: Guess how many separate thought fragments can appear during ten actual seconds.

rituals.catch: Compare mental speed with external time.
rituals.reveal: Internal urgency can accelerate while the clock remains completely unimpressed.
rituals.mindBend: A fast mind does not make the world move faster.

rituals.name: TONGUE PARKING SPOT
rituals.title: TONGUE PARKING SPOT
rituals.targetPattern: Tongue tension outside awareness
rituals.target_pattern: Tongue tension outside awareness
rituals.precise_subpattern: Tongue tension outside awareness
rituals.vibeLine: Tiny muscle, surprisingly committed to the crisis.
rituals.hook: Your tongue may be attending a meeting nobody invited it to.
rituals.predict: Guess whether it is pressing, bracing, floating, or resting.
rituals.play: Notice where the tongue is touching right now. Let it rest loosely in the floor of the mouth for three seconds. Don’t force anything else to relax.
rituals.catch: Compare the jaw, throat and face before and after that one tiny relocation.
rituals.reveal: Small hidden muscles can participate in a whole-body sense of effort.
rituals.mindBend: Sometimes “I’m tense” includes one very enthusiastic tongue.

rituals.targetPattern: Neutral moments ignored between stress spikes
rituals.target_pattern: Neutral moments ignored between stress spikes
rituals.precise_subpattern: Neutral moments ignored between stress spikes
rituals.vibeLine: Stress said “constant.” The footage contains edits.
rituals.hook: We are not looking for peace.
rituals.predict: Guess whether there is any half-second today when the discomfort changes, dips, shifts location, or gets interrupted.
rituals.play: For 20 sec, watch only for change—not improvement. A blink, swallow, sound, movement, or thought switch counts if the experience is different.
rituals.catch: Catch the first moment that proves the state is not perfectly continuous.
rituals.reveal: The nervous system can feel constant while actually changing in tiny increments.
rituals.mindBend: You do not need calm to prove that “unchanging” was an illusion.

rituals.name: ONE SQUARE CENTIMETRE
rituals.title: ONE SQUARE CENTIMETRE
rituals.targetPattern: Complex scenes maintaining cognitive load
rituals.target_pattern: Complex scenes maintaining cognitive load
rituals.precise_subpattern: Complex scenes maintaining cognitive load
rituals.vibeLine: Your worry lost screen time to one square centimetre.
rituals.hook: Shrink the visual world to something absurdly small.
rituals.predict: Guess whether a tiny patch contains more detail than you normally notice.
rituals.play: Pick a patch about the size of a fingernail on any safe object. Spend 10 sec finding three details inside only that patch: colour variation, edge, fibre, scratch, light.
rituals.catch: Notice what happened to the rest of the room while the patch became detailed.
rituals.reveal: Attention can trade breadth for detail on purpose instead of being dragged there by worry.
rituals.mindBend: A tiny piece of reality can be larger than a whole thought when you actually look.

rituals.name: THE ROOM DISAPPEARS
rituals.title: THE ROOM DISAPPEARS
rituals.targetPattern: Automatic visual interruptions ignored
rituals.target_pattern: Automatic visual interruptions ignored
rituals.precise_subpattern: Automatic visual interruptions ignored
rituals.vibeLine: The room vanished six times and somehow nobody panicked.
rituals.hook: Your world goes dark repeatedly and you barely notice.
rituals.predict: Guess how many blinks happen in twenty seconds.
rituals.play: For 20 sec, notice each blink as a tiny visual cut—no need to change the rate. Count only if easy.
rituals.catch: Catch the fact that perception feels continuous despite repeated gaps.
rituals.reveal: The brain stitches interruptions into a stable scene.
rituals.mindBend: Continuous experience is partly a very convincing edit.

rituals.name: SOCK VANISHING ACT
rituals.title: SOCK VANISHING ACT
rituals.targetPattern: Constant touch fading from awareness
rituals.target_pattern: Constant touch fading from awareness
rituals.precise_subpattern: Constant touch fading from awareness
rituals.vibeLine: Your nervous system muted a perfectly real sensation for convenience.
rituals.hook: Your clothes are touching you right now.
rituals.predict: Guess which clothing contact you can notice fastest.
rituals.play: Notice one constant contact—sock, waistband, sleeve, watch, chair. Hold attention there for five seconds, then let it go.
rituals.catch: Catch how easily the sensation returns and fades again.
rituals.reveal: The nervous system down-weights constant, non-changing input.
rituals.mindBend: Not noticing something does not mean your body stopped sensing it.

rituals.vibeLine: Your body is balancing via tiny secret negotiations.
rituals.hook: Standing still is not actually still.
rituals.predict: If safe to stand, predict whether your body moves at all while you feel stationary.

rituals.catch: Catch movement that normally gets edited out of the idea of “still.”
rituals.reveal: Balance is active adjustment, not frozen stability.
rituals.mindBend: Stillness can be made of constant tiny corrections.

rituals.vibeLine: Same world, different sensor angle.
rituals.hook: Move only your head and the sensory world reorganises.
rituals.predict: Guess which direction contains the most sound or visual activity.
rituals.play: Slowly turn your head left, centre, right once. At each point, notice one different sound or visual detail. Keep the body still if comfortable.
rituals.catch: Notice how changing orientation changes what becomes salient.
rituals.reveal: The environment can feel different because the sampling angle changed.
rituals.mindBend: Sometimes “the world feels intense” includes where your sensors are pointed.

Room got remixed by a tiny head turn.

Move only your head and the sensory world reorganises.
jolly.ritualCard:
Move only your head and the sensory world reorganises.
Slowly turn your head left, centre, right once. At each point, notice one different sound or visual detail. Keep the body still if comfortable.
Guess which direction contains the most sound or visual activity.
Notice how changing orientation changes what becomes salient. The environment can feel different because the sampling angle changed.
↻ TURN THE ROOM

rituals.name: EDGE DISAPPEARING TRICK
rituals.title: EDGE DISAPPEARING TRICK
rituals.targetPattern: Attention assuming a stable visual stimulus is continuously noticed
rituals.target_pattern: Attention assuming a stable visual stimulus is continuously noticed
rituals.precise_subpattern: Attention assuming a stable visual stimulus is continuously noticed
rituals.vibeLine: Still there. Less reported. Sneaky.
rituals.hook: Your eyes are about to prove they stop reporting things that stay still.
rituals.predict: Guess whether a fixed edge stays equally vivid when you stare beside it for ten seconds.
rituals.play: Pick a harmless stationary edge or small mark. Look just beside it without moving your eyes much. Notice whether the edge fades, blurs, or becomes less prominent.
rituals.catch: Catch the moment the unchanging thing becomes less available.
rituals.reveal: Sensory systems prioritise change over perfect continuous reporting.
rituals.mindBend: Something can stay present while your brain quietly stops shouting about it.

rituals.name: LEFT HAND / RIGHT HAND
rituals.title: LEFT HAND / RIGHT HAND
rituals.targetPattern: Tension baseline hidden until left-right comparison
rituals.target_pattern: Tension baseline hidden until left-right comparison
rituals.precise_subpattern: Tension baseline hidden until left-right comparison
rituals.vibeLine: One hand may have been working a second job.
rituals.hook: Your two hands may be living different lives.
rituals.predict: Guess which hand is holding more unnecessary effort.
rituals.play: Let both hands rest. Without moving much, compare finger curl, pressure, temperature, and weight left versus right. Soften only the tenser side by five percent.
rituals.catch: Notice how comparison reveals effort that felt invisible alone.
rituals.reveal: The nervous system notices contrast better than baseline.

rituals.name: FIND THE QUIETEST NOISE
rituals.title: FIND THE QUIETEST NOISE
rituals.targetPattern: Silence imagined as absence rather than layered low-level sound
rituals.target_pattern: Silence imagined as absence rather than layered low-level sound
rituals.precise_subpattern: Silence imagined as absence rather than layered low-level sound
rituals.vibeLine: Background noise just revealed its basement.
rituals.hook: Silence is rarely empty.
rituals.predict: Guess whether you can find a sound quieter than the one you currently call background.
rituals.play: Listen for 10 sec, repeatedly choosing a quieter sound than the last one: hum, fabric, distant traffic, breath, electronics, room tone.
rituals.catch: Notice how “silence” gains layers when attention changes resolution.

rituals.name: HORIZON SWEEP
rituals.title: HORIZON SWEEP
rituals.targetPattern: Mental fixation mirrored by rigid gaze
rituals.target_pattern: Mental fixation mirrored by rigid gaze
rituals.precise_subpattern: Mental fixation mirrored by rigid gaze
rituals.vibeLine: The thought wanted tunnel vision. Your eyes declined.
rituals.hook: Let your eyes move before your thought does.
rituals.predict: Guess whether slow horizontal eye movement changes the feeling of being mentally stuck.
rituals.play: Keep your head mostly still. Slowly move your gaze from the far left of the room to the far right and back once, noticing objects you cross.
rituals.catch: Check if the mental scene feels equally narrow afterward.
rituals.reveal: Visual exploration and attentional breadth are linked.
rituals.mindBend: A stuck thought can happen inside a world your eyes have stopped exploring.
rituals.ritualCard:
Let your eyes move before your thought does.
Keep your head mostly still. Slowly move your gaze from the far left of the room to the far right and back once, noticing objects you cross.
Guess whether slow horizontal eye movement changes the feeling of being mentally stuck.
Check if the mental scene feels equally narrow afterward. Visual exploration and attentional breadth are linked.

Let your eyes move before your thought does.

rituals.name: STANDING IS TINY FALLING
rituals.title: STANDING IS TINY FALLING
rituals.targetPattern: Balance experienced as static rather than continuous correction
rituals.target_pattern: Balance experienced as static rather than continuous correction
rituals.precise_subpattern: Balance experienced as static rather than continuous correction
rituals.vibeLine: Standing still is apparently a very quiet action sequence.
rituals.hook: Standing still is less still than it looks.
rituals.predict: Guess whether your body is perfectly motionless while standing safely.
rituals.play: If safe, stand with normal stance near support. Notice tiny shifts at ankles, feet, hips. Don’t try to stop them.
rituals.catch: Catch the continuous micro-corrections keeping you upright.
rituals.reveal: Stability is often active adjustment, not frozen stillness.
rituals.mindBend: Calm does not have to mean zero movement.

HOOK
Standing still is less still than it looks.

PREDICT
Guess whether your body is perfectly motionless while standing safely.

PLAY

CATCH
Catch the continuous micro-corrections keeping you upright.

REVEAL
Stability is often active adjustment, not frozen stillness.

MIND BEND
Calm does not have to mean zero movement.

rituals.name: EYES CLOSED SIZE SHIFT
rituals.title: EYES CLOSED SIZE SHIFT
rituals.targetPattern: Vision overriding other spatial cues
rituals.target_pattern: Vision overriding other spatial cues
rituals.precise_subpattern: Vision overriding other spatial cues
rituals.vibeLine: Same hand. Slightly different internal cartography.
rituals.hook: Your body has a size map even when your eyes are off duty.
rituals.predict: Guess how large your hands feel with eyes open versus closed.
rituals.play: Look at one hand for three seconds. Close your eyes and feel only its boundaries for five seconds. Open and compare the sensed hand with the seen hand.
rituals.catch: Notice any shift in size, shape, weight, or vividness.
rituals.reveal: The brain builds body experience from multiple senses that do not always agree perfectly.
rituals.mindBend: What you feel as “my body” is an ongoing negotiation between signals.

rituals.hook: Attention is a zoom lens.
rituals.predict: Guess whether one mild neutral sensation feels larger after ten seconds of focused attention.
rituals.play: Choose a harmless sensation—finger pressure, shoe contact, hand warmth. Focus narrowly on it for 10 sec. Widen attention to the whole room for ten.
rituals.catch: Compare the sensation’s apparent size or importance across the two attention widths.
rituals.reveal: Attention can magnify a sensation without changing its underlying cause.
rituals.mindBend: Bigger in awareness is not automatically bigger in the body.

rituals.name: ONE FINGER LIFT
rituals.title: ONE FINGER LIFT
rituals.targetPattern: Movement expected to require more effort than it does
rituals.target_pattern: Movement expected to require more effort than it does
rituals.precise_subpattern: Movement expected to require more effort than it does
rituals.vibeLine: Effort forecast was dramatically overfunded.
rituals.hook: Your body prediction may be charging full-task prices for tiny movements.
rituals.predict: Guess how effortful it will feel to lift one finger slowly.
rituals.play: Rest a hand. Lift only one finger a centimetre, lower it, and notice the actual effort. Repeat with a different finger.
rituals.catch: Compare predicted effort with the ridiculously small movement.
rituals.reveal: The brain can bundle “movement” into a larger effort forecast than the action requires.
rituals.mindBend: Tiny motion can be easier than the story attached to moving.

unfiltered.openingLine:
Sometimes move one damn finger before believing the whole damn effort story.

Your body prediction may be charging full-task prices for tiny movements.
unfiltered.ritualCard:
Your body prediction may be charging full-task prices for tiny movements.
Rest a hand. Lift only one finger a centimetre, lower it, and notice the actual effort. Repeat with a different finger.
Guess how effortful it will feel to lift one finger slowly.
Compare predicted effort with the ridiculously small movement. The brain can bundle “movement” into a larger effort forecast than the action requires.
↻ ONE FINGER LIFT

rituals.name: SENSE CHANNEL SURF
rituals.title: SENSE CHANNEL SURF
rituals.targetPattern: One sensory channel monopolising awareness
rituals.target_pattern: One sensory channel monopolising awareness
rituals.precise_subpattern: One sensory channel monopolising awareness
rituals.vibeLine: Your brain has more than one channel after all.
rituals.hook: We are changing channels, not fixing the programme.
rituals.predict: Guess which sense is currently dominating your awareness.
rituals.play: Spend three seconds each on sight, sound, touch, temperature, and body position. No interpretation—just switch channels.
rituals.catch: Notice which channel is easiest to enter and hardest to leave.
rituals.reveal: Attention can move across sensory systems even while thoughts continue.
rituals.mindBend: Your mind is not a one-channel broadcast.

Stop letting one damn channel pretend it owns the television.

HOOK
We are changing channels, not fixing the programme.

PREDICT
Guess which sense is currently dominating your awareness.

PLAY

CATCH
Notice which channel is easiest to enter and hardest to leave.

REVEAL
Attention can move across sensory systems even while thoughts continue.

MIND BEND
Your mind is not a one-channel broadcast.

rituals.name: THE PHONE CHANGED WEIGHT
rituals.title: THE PHONE CHANGED WEIGHT
rituals.targetPattern: Weight judgment shifted by immediately prior load
rituals.target_pattern: Weight judgment shifted by immediately prior load
rituals.precise_subpattern: Weight judgment shifted by immediately prior load
rituals.vibeLine: Your phone lost zero grams and gained a new vibe.
rituals.hook: The object may feel lighter without losing a gram.
rituals.predict: Guess whether your phone or another safe light object feels different after holding something heavier for a few seconds.
rituals.play: Hold a comfortably heavier safe object, put it down, then pick up the lighter object. Compare with its normal feel.
rituals.catch: Notice the contrast effect in your muscles and perception.
rituals.reveal: Sensation is judged relative to what came immediately before.
rituals.mindBend: Feeling lighter does not mean becoming lighter.

cheeky.play: Hold a comfortably heavier safe object, put it down, then pick up the lighter object. Compare with its normal feel.
cheeky.catch: Notice the contrast effect in your muscles and perception.
cheeky.reveal: Sensation is judged relative to what came immediately before.
cheeky.mindBend: Feeling lighter does not mean becoming lighter.
cheeky.safety:
PAUSE
Keep the hold light and reversible. The exercise should widen perspective, not pressure you to deny facts or push through rising distress. Leave room for new evidence after the exercise instead of treating the result as final.

rituals.name: RUBBER PENCIL LIE
rituals.title: RUBBER PENCIL LIE
rituals.targetPattern: Rapid small movement making a rigid object appear flexible
rituals.target_pattern: Rapid small movement making a rigid object appear flexible
rituals.precise_subpattern: Rapid small movement making a rigid object appear flexible
rituals.vibeLine: Physics is fine. Your visual system got creative.
rituals.hook: A rigid pencil is about to look like rubber.
rituals.predict: Guess whether a straight pen can look bendy without actually bending.
rituals.play: Hold a pen loosely near one end and wiggle your hand quickly up and down with a small motion. Watch the pen's middle.
rituals.catch: Catch the apparent bend.
rituals.reveal: Vision integrates motion over time and can misread rigid movement as flexible shape.
rituals.mindBend: What looks obvious can be a timing trick in perception.

rituals.vibeLine: Eye open. Thumb gone. Very rude.
rituals.hook: Your eye has a blind spot.
rituals.predict: Guess whether a small target can disappear while your eye remains open.

rituals.reveal: The brain fills missing visual information so smoothly that the gap usually feels nonexistent.
rituals.mindBend: A complete-looking experience can contain invisible missing data.

rituals.name: COLOUR LEAVES BEFORE SHAPE
rituals.title: COLOUR LEAVES BEFORE SHAPE
rituals.targetPattern: Colour information degrading before shape in peripheral vision
rituals.target_pattern: Colour information degrading before shape in peripheral vision
rituals.precise_subpattern: Colour information degrading before shape in peripheral vision
rituals.vibeLine: Shape arrived before full-colour service.
rituals.hook: Your peripheral vision is less colourful than it feels.
rituals.predict: Guess whether you lose colour or object shape first as something moves toward the edge of vision.
rituals.play: Fix your gaze straight ahead. Move a colourful safe object slowly from beside your head toward the front without following it with your eyes. Notice when colour becomes clear.
rituals.catch: Catch that you can detect 'something' before you can identify its colour well.
rituals.reveal: Peripheral vision prioritises different information than central vision.
rituals.mindBend: Your visual field feels uniformly detailed because the brain stitches unequal zones together.

rituals.vibeLine: Red objects filed a complaint about being ignored.
rituals.hook: Attention can make obvious things temporarily irrelevant enough to disappear.
rituals.predict: Guess how many blue objects you can find in ten seconds.

rituals.name: EYES-CLOSED NOSE LANDING
rituals.title: EYES-CLOSED NOSE LANDING
rituals.targetPattern: Movement endpoint predicted before visual correction
rituals.target_pattern: Movement endpoint predicted before visual correction
rituals.precise_subpattern: Movement endpoint predicted before visual correction
rituals.vibeLine: No camera, still mostly found the nose.
rituals.hook: Your hand can find your face without GPS.
rituals.predict: Guess exactly where your fingertip will land when you touch your nose with eyes closed.
rituals.play: Close your eyes, slowly bring one index finger to the tip of your nose, then open your eyes to check the landing.
rituals.catch: Notice the tiny accuracy or error produced without visual guidance.
rituals.reveal: The body constantly predicts limb position from internal signals.
rituals.mindBend: Even simple movement is guided by an invisible model, not direct certainty.

rituals.vibeLine: Nothing inside necessarily changed; the room got quieter.

rituals.mindBend: A signal can feel stronger because competition became quieter.

rituals.name: COMPLEMENTARY COLOUR ECHO
rituals.title: COMPLEMENTARY COLOUR ECHO
rituals.targetPattern: Recently viewed colour producing an opposite-colour percept after removal
rituals.target_pattern: Recently viewed colour producing an opposite-colour percept after removal
rituals.precise_subpattern: Recently viewed colour producing an opposite-colour percept after removal
rituals.vibeLine: Object gone. Visual system still filing paperwork.
rituals.hook: Your eyes can keep a colour after the object is gone.
rituals.predict: Guess what colour ghost appears after staring at one safe coloured object.
rituals.play: Look at a non-bright coloured object for about fifteen seconds, then shift to a plain white or light wall. Don’t use lights or the sun.
rituals.catch: Catch the faint complementary colour that may appear.
rituals.reveal: Visual receptors adapt, and the contrast system keeps processing after the stimulus leaves.
rituals.mindBend: Seeing something after it is gone can be a property of the visual system, not of the world.

jolly.predict: Guess what colour ghost appears after staring at one safe coloured object.
jolly.play: Look at a non-bright coloured object for about fifteen seconds, then shift to a plain white or light wall. Don’t use lights or the sun.
jolly.catch: Catch the faint complementary colour that may appear.
jolly.reveal: Visual receptors adapt, and the contrast system keeps processing after the stimulus leaves.
jolly.mindBend: Seeing something after it is gone can be a property of the visual system, not of the world.
jolly.safety:
PAUSE
Use an ordinary non-glare object and a comfortable gaze; never use the sun, bright lamps, lasers or anything painful to look at. Stop for eye pain, headache, dizziness or a visual effect that lingers unexpectedly.
jolly.targetPattern: Recently viewed colour producing an opposite-colour percept after removal
jolly.theoryBackbone: Visual adaptation; opponent-process colour vision; afterimage
jolly.mechanismFingerprint: Briefly adapt to a safe coloured surface, then view a neutral field to reveal a complementary afterimage caused by receptor/opponent adaptation.

rituals.precise_subpattern: Arrowhead context changing perceived line length
rituals.vibeLine: Same line, different accessories, whole new attitude.

rituals.predict: Guess which looks longer: a line with arrowheads pointing out or one with arrowheads pointing in.

rituals.reveal: Surrounding geometry changes perceived length.
rituals.mindBend: Your eyes can be wrong with confidence while the ruler stays boring.

rituals.vibeLine: Same circle, different social circle.
rituals.hook: A circle can look bigger simply because its neighbours are tiny.
rituals.predict: Guess which identical centre circle will look larger: one surrounded by small circles or large circles.

rituals.precise_subpattern: Vertical extent perceived as longer than equal horizontal extent
rituals.vibeLine: Same centimetres. Different ego.
rituals.hook: Equal lines can feel unequal because one stands up.
rituals.predict: Guess whether a vertical line or equal horizontal line looks longer.
rituals.play: Draw an L shape with one vertical and one horizontal line of exactly equal measured length. Look first, measure second.
rituals.catch: Check if the vertical line feels taller than the horizontal feels wide.
rituals.reveal: Orientation affects perceived extent.
rituals.mindBend: The eye does not carry a perfect internal ruler.

rituals.vibeLine: Your palm just got special effects.

rituals.predict: Guess whether you can make a hole appear through your own hand.

rituals.mindBend: A unified visual world can contain pieces that never existed together.

unfiltered.openingLine:
Your damn brain punched a hole in a damn hand that stayed perfectly solid.

Your brain is about to merge two incompatible views into one ridiculous picture.
unfiltered.ritualCard:
Your brain is about to merge two incompatible views into one ridiculous picture.
Roll a sheet of paper into a tube. Look through it with one eye at a distant object. Hold your other open hand beside the tube, close to the far end. Keep both eyes open.
Guess whether you can make a hole appear through your own hand.
Catch the apparent hole through your palm where the tube view merges with the hand view. The brain combines information from two eyes into one best-guess scene.
↻ HOLE IN YOUR HAND

rituals.targetPattern: Binocular aim depending more on one eye
rituals.target_pattern: Binocular aim depending more on one eye
rituals.precise_subpattern: Binocular aim depending more on one eye
rituals.vibeLine: One eye apparently has seniority.
rituals.hook: Two eyes, one tiny executive decision.
rituals.predict: Guess which eye your brain trusts more for aiming.
rituals.play: Make a small triangle with your hands and centre a distant object inside it with both eyes open. Close one eye, then the other.
rituals.catch: Notice which eye keeps the object centred.
rituals.reveal: Binocular vision often has a dominant eye for alignment tasks.
rituals.mindBend: Two equal-looking sensors can contribute differently to one experience.

rituals.vibeLine: Tiny thumb, huge building, same patch of vision.

rituals.predict: Guess how many distant objects your thumb can visually cover at arm's length.

rituals.reveal: The brain adjusts perceived size using distance information.
rituals.mindBend: What reaches the eye is not the same as what you experience as size.

cheeky.openingLine:
Tiny thumb, huge building, same patch of vision.

Your thumb can cover a far object without becoming enormous.
cheeky.ritualCard:
Your thumb can cover a far object without becoming enormous.
Hold your thumb out and use it to cover a distant safe object such as a door, sign, or building section. Compare physical size with visual angle.
Guess how many distant objects your thumb can visually cover at arm's length.
Catch how tiny retinal size does not make the distant object feel thumb-sized. The brain adjusts perceived size using distance information.

rituals.name: VASE OR FACES?
rituals.title: VASE OR FACES?
rituals.targetPattern: Same visual input supporting two alternating organisations
rituals.target_pattern: Same visual input supporting two alternating organisations
rituals.precise_subpattern: Same visual input supporting two alternating organisations
rituals.vibeLine: Pixels refused to pick a side.
rituals.hook: One drawing can contain two realities without changing a pixel.
rituals.predict: Guess whether you see the vase or the two faces first.
rituals.play: Draw two opposing face profiles with a narrow symmetrical gap between them, or picture the classic vase/faces figure. Alternate seeing the centre as object, then the sides as objects.
rituals.catch: Catch the flip even though the lines stay fixed.
rituals.reveal: Perception chooses an organisation, not just a collection of edges.
rituals.mindBend: The same data can support more than one stable interpretation.

rituals.name: CUBE FLIP
rituals.title: CUBE FLIP
rituals.targetPattern: Depth orientation flipping in an unchanged wireframe
rituals.target_pattern: Depth orientation flipping in an unchanged wireframe
rituals.precise_subpattern: Depth orientation flipping in an unchanged wireframe
rituals.vibeLine: Same lines. New front wall.
rituals.hook: A cube can turn inside out without moving.
rituals.predict: Guess which face of a simple wireframe cube will feel closest.
rituals.play: Draw or imagine a Necker cube—two offset squares joined at the corners. Stare gently and try to let the front face flip.
rituals.catch: Catch the sudden depth reversal with no line changing.
rituals.reveal: Ambiguous sensory input can support competing perceptual models.
rituals.mindBend: The brain can switch realities while the evidence stays identical.

rituals.vibeLine: Clock said identical. Experience disagreed.
rituals.hook: Ten seconds can feel like different sizes.
rituals.predict: Guess which feels longer: ten seconds of counting three changing things or ten seconds staring at one still object.
rituals.play: Do one ten-second interval tracking three small changes around you. One ten-second interval on a single still point. Use the same clock.
rituals.catch: Compare subjective length with identical clock time.
rituals.reveal: Event density influences experienced duration.
rituals.mindBend: Time on the clock can stay fixed while time in experience stretches.

unfiltered.play: Do one ten-second interval tracking three small changes around you. One ten-second interval on a single still point. Use the same clock.
unfiltered.catch: Compare subjective length with identical clock time.
unfiltered.reveal: Event density influences experienced duration.
unfiltered.mindBend: Time on the clock can stay fixed while time in experience stretches.
unfiltered.safety:

unfiltered.targetPattern: Busy intervals feeling longer in the moment than empty ones
unfiltered.theoryBackbone: Time perception; event density; prospective duration

rituals.targetPattern: Grouping changing apparent memory capacity
rituals.target_pattern: Grouping changing apparent memory capacity
rituals.precise_subpattern: Grouping changing apparent memory capacity
rituals.vibeLine: Ten items just became three without deleting anything.
rituals.hook: Memory size changes when the pieces learn to travel together.
rituals.predict: Guess which is easier: remembering 2-0-2-6-0-9-1-8-4-2 or 2026 / 0918 / 42.
rituals.play: Take a long sequence of digits or letters. Read it once as separate items, then reorganise it into meaningful or rhythmic chunks.
rituals.catch: Notice how the same information occupies fewer mental slots.
rituals.reveal: Working memory capacity depends partly on how information is grouped.
rituals.mindBend: The amount of data stayed the same; the number of mental objects changed.

cheeky.openingLine:
Open eyes, missing update.

Your eyes can miss a big change if the scene gets interrupted at the right moment.
cheeky.ritualCard:
Your eyes can miss a big change if the scene gets interrupted at the right moment.
Arrange three harmless objects. Look away, move one slightly, then look back. If someone can help, let them do the move while you turn.
Guess whether you would notice an object moved if you looked away briefly.
Catch how attention, not just vision, determines change detection. Seeing a scene does not mean every feature is continuously represented.

rituals.vibeLine: Second target arrived during paperwork.
rituals.hook: Attention can catch one thing and temporarily miss the next.

rituals.mindBend: Missing the second thing can be timing, not carelessness.

rituals.name: THE WORD FIGHTS THE COLOUR
rituals.title: THE WORD FIGHTS THE COLOUR
rituals.targetPattern: Word meaning competing with ink colour
rituals.target_pattern: Word meaning competing with ink colour
rituals.precise_subpattern: Word meaning competing with ink colour
rituals.vibeLine: Word said one thing, ink said another, brain filed a complaint.
rituals.hook: Your brain reads before you ask it to.
rituals.predict: Guess how much slower it feels to name the ink colour of the word RED printed in blue.
rituals.play: Write colour words in mismatched pen colours. Name the ink colours, not the words.
rituals.catch: Notice the tug of the automatic reading response.
rituals.reveal: Automatic processes can interfere with intentional ones.
rituals.mindBend: Effort can come from competition, not weakness.
rituals.ritualCard:
Your brain reads before you ask it to.

rituals.target_pattern: Reciprocal taps feeling unequal and escalating
rituals.precise_subpattern: Reciprocal taps feeling unequal and escalating
rituals.vibeLine: Both sides can sincerely say 'you started it harder.'

rituals.name: PAUSE DISTORTS DISTANCE
rituals.title: PAUSE DISTORTS DISTANCE
rituals.targetPattern: Timing between stimuli changing perceived spatial distance
rituals.target_pattern: Timing between stimuli changing perceived spatial distance
rituals.precise_subpattern: Timing between stimuli changing perceived spatial distance
rituals.vibeLine: Same distance, different pause, different feeling.
rituals.hook: Two equal distances can feel unequal when the timing changes.
rituals.predict: Guess which gap feels longer when the pause before crossing it is longer.
rituals.play: Imagine three equally spaced taps or lights. Let the time gap between first-second be short and second-third long. Notice which spatial interval feels larger.
rituals.catch: Catch time leaking into distance judgment.
rituals.reveal: Perceived space and time influence each other.
rituals.mindBend: Your internal ruler and clock are not independent departments.

rituals.title: DISTANCE DISTORTS DURATION
rituals.targetPattern: Spatial distance changing perceived time interval
rituals.target_pattern: Spatial distance changing perceived time interval
rituals.precise_subpattern: Spatial distance changing perceived time interval
rituals.vibeLine: Farther looked slower without a slower timer.
rituals.hook: Your clock can be fooled by distance.
rituals.predict: Guess which equal time interval feels longer when the second event happens farther away.
rituals.play: Imagine three flashes with equal timing but different spatial gaps. Compare the interval spanning the larger distance with the smaller one.
rituals.catch: Check if farther travel feels like more time.
rituals.reveal: Spatial separation can bias perceived duration.
rituals.mindBend: The brain's clock borrows assumptions from movement through space.

rituals.name: STILL LIGHT, MOVING EYE
rituals.title: STILL LIGHT, MOVING EYE
rituals.targetPattern: A stationary light in darkness seeming to move
rituals.target_pattern: A stationary light in darkness seeming to move
rituals.precise_subpattern: A stationary light in darkness seeming to move
rituals.vibeLine: Maybe the dot moved. Maybe your eyes did.
rituals.hook: A stationary point can seem to wander when the world gives you no reference frame.
rituals.predict: Guess whether a tiny fixed light in a dark room would feel perfectly still.
rituals.play: Safely look at a small stationary indicator light in a dim room for a few seconds without straining. Notice any apparent drift. Stop if uncomfortable.
rituals.catch: Catch movement that may come from tiny eye movements and missing references.
rituals.reveal: Perception of motion depends on reference frames.
rituals.mindBend: When context disappears, the brain can mistake its own movement for the world's.

cheeky.displayName: THE BEEP CONTINUES BEHIND THE NOISE
cheeky.openingLine:
Silence broke the tone; noise strangely repaired it.

Your brain can fill in a missing sound if the interruption has a plausible cover.
cheeky.ritualCard:
Your brain can fill in a missing sound if the interruption has a plausible cover.
Imagine or safely compare a tone–noise–tone sequence with a tone–silence–tone sequence.
Guess whether a steady tone interrupted by a burst of noise feels more continuous than one interrupted by silence.
Notice how noise can make the tone feel as though it continued behind it. Perception reconstructs likely hidden continuity.

rituals.name: THE SHADOW CHANGES THE STORY
rituals.title: THE SHADOW CHANGES THE STORY
rituals.targetPattern: Contextual lighting making identical shades look different
rituals.target_pattern: Contextual lighting making identical shades look different
rituals.precise_subpattern: Contextual lighting making identical shades look different
rituals.vibeLine: Same square, different imagined sun.
rituals.hook: A shadow can convince you two identical shades are different objects.
rituals.predict: Guess whether a square in shadow looks lighter than an equal square outside it.
rituals.play: Draw a simple checker pattern with a broad fake shadow, or picture the classic checker-shadow illusion. Compare two equal-value squares across the lighting context.
rituals.catch: Notice how the brain corrects for assumed illumination.
rituals.reveal: Vision estimates surface colour by factoring in lighting.
rituals.mindBend: You do not see raw brightness; you see a corrected guess about the world.

rituals.title: TEMPERATURES DON'T JUST AVERAGE
rituals.targetPattern: Mixed warm and cool inputs combining into a qualitatively different sensation
rituals.target_pattern: Mixed warm and cool inputs combining into a qualitatively different sensation
rituals.precise_subpattern: Mixed warm and cool inputs combining into a qualitatively different sensation
rituals.vibeLine: Warm plus cool is not obliged to equal boring.
rituals.hook: The nervous system does not always combine temperature like a calculator.
rituals.predict: Guess whether mixed warm and cool contact must feel exactly lukewarm.
rituals.play: Without using extreme temperatures, compare one mildly cool safe object and one mildly warm safe object separately. Imagine them patterned together rather than averaged.
rituals.catch: Notice the assumption that combined sensation should be arithmetic.
rituals.reveal: Thermal perception arises from interacting neural channels, not simple temperature averaging.
rituals.mindBend: Two safe sensations can combine into a new experience rather than a midpoint.

The nervous system does not always combine temperature like a calculator.
Without using extreme temperatures, compare one mildly cool safe object and one mildly warm safe object separately. Imagine them patterned together rather than averaged.

rituals.vibeLine: Straight route, wrong re-entry point.

rituals.predict: Guess where a diagonal line should continue after passing behind a rectangle.

rituals.catch: Notice the alignment error.
rituals.reveal: Occlusion and angle context distort extrapolation.

rituals.vibeLine: Last frame quietly rolled forward.

rituals.catch: Notice any forward drift in the remembered endpoint.
rituals.reveal: Memory for dynamic scenes often extrapolates motion.
rituals.mindBend: Your mind can remember where the object was going, not only where it was.

rituals.vibeLine: Same circle, different landlord.

rituals.predict: Guess which identical centre circle looks larger: one inside a tight ring or one inside a huge ring.

rituals.catch: Notice the centre circles appear unequal.

rituals.mindBend: A boundary around something can change the size you experience, not the size that exists.

rituals.name: BORDER BRIGHTNESS HACK
rituals.title: BORDER BRIGHTNESS HACK
rituals.targetPattern: Two equal-brightness regions looking different because of a narrow edge gradient
rituals.target_pattern: Two equal-brightness regions looking different because of a narrow edge gradient
rituals.precise_subpattern: Two equal-brightness regions looking different because of a narrow edge gradient
rituals.vibeLine: Edge did the drama; surface got the reputation.
rituals.hook: A tiny boundary can make entire regions look lighter or darker.
rituals.predict: Guess whether two broad grey areas with equal centres can look different if their shared edge has a light-dark gradient.
rituals.play: Imagine two equal grey panels touching, with a narrow bright strip on one side of the border and dark strip on the other. Cover the edge mentally or physically.
rituals.catch: Catch the large-area brightness difference collapse when the edge disappears.
rituals.reveal: The visual system infers surface brightness strongly from local edge structure.
rituals.mindBend: A narrow edge can colour your experience of a huge area.

rituals.vibeLine: White interior, suspiciously tinted experience.

rituals.reveal: Contour interactions can create long-range colour filling-in.

rituals.title: ORDER CHANGES THE COMPARISON
rituals.targetPattern: Two equal stimuli being judged differently because one came first or second
rituals.target_pattern: Two equal stimuli being judged differently because one came first or second
rituals.precise_subpattern: Two equal stimuli being judged differently because one came first or second
rituals.vibeLine: First became benchmark; second got reviewed.
rituals.hook: Equal experiences can stop feeling equal because one arrived first.
rituals.predict: Guess whether the second of two equal waits feels longer, shorter, or simply different after you have a reference.
rituals.play: Compare two equal timed intervals separated by a short break. Judge which felt longer before checking the clock.
rituals.catch: Check if order creates a directional bias.
rituals.reveal: Sequential comparison can distort perceived magnitude even when stimuli match.
rituals.mindBend: The first event becomes a reference point the second never gets to be.

Draw a jagged starburst and a rounded blob. Assign the two nonsense labels before overthinking.

rituals.vibeLine: Two leans left; nine has a right-side preference.
rituals.hook: Numbers may be sitting on an invisible line in your head.
rituals.predict: Guess which side feels more natural for 2 and which for 9.
rituals.play: Imagine numbers 1 through 9 appearing one at a time. Quickly point left for 'small' and right for 'large,' then reverse the mapping and notice which direction feels stranger.
rituals.catch: Catch the spatial habit attached to magnitude.
rituals.reveal: Number magnitude is often mapped spatially in cognition.
rituals.mindBend: Abstract quantities can inherit physical direction.

Still · Calm · NUMBERS HAVE A HIDDEN DIRECTION
VIBE: UNFILTERED

Your damn numbers may be living on a damn hidden line.

HOOK
Numbers may be sitting on an invisible line in your head.

PREDICT
Guess which side feels more natural for 2 and which for 9.

PLAY
Imagine numbers 1 through 9 appearing one at a time. Quickly point left for 'small' and right for 'large,' then reverse the mapping and notice which direction feels stranger.

CATCH
Catch the spatial habit attached to magnitude.

REVEAL
Number magnitude is often mapped spatially in cognition.

MIND BEND
Abstract quantities can inherit physical direction.
